content: Start a new scene and set the camera rotation to isometric (Image 1). With the Camera selected, [k]Numpad0[/k] to toggle the camera view and [k]G[/k] the camera until the cube is centered in the view (Image 2). In the Data Properties tab, set [k]Lens > Type > Orthograpic[/k] (Image 3).

image.caption: Image 1 - Starting a new scene and setting the camera rotation to isometric
Image 2 - Selecting the Camera, toggling the camera view and moving the camera until the cube is centered in the view
Image 3 - Going to the Data Properties tab and setting the Lens Type to Orthographic

content: With the cube as the active object, [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode, select the bottom vertices and [k]G,Z,1[/k] up to the World Origin (Image 4). Select the top face, [k]E,RMB[/k] [k]S[/k] to scale it out in place (Image 5). Clean it up so that the extra faces are gone and you have only five faces on top (Image 6). Select the faces around the edge and [k]E[/k] to extrude them down (Image 7). Delete the inner faces around the top (Image 8).

image.caption: Image 4 - Going into Edit Mode with the cube as the active object, selecting the bottom vertices and moving them up to the World Origin
Image 5 - Selecting the top face and scaling it out in place
Image 6 - Cleaning it up so that the extra faces are gone and only five faces remain on top
Image 7 - Selecting the faces around the edge and extruding them down
Image 8 - Deleting the inner faces around the top

content: [k]F[/k] to fill in the empty space up top (Image 9). Select all side edges going around the tiles (Image 10) and [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel them with two segments (Image 11). Select all faces along the beveled edges (Image 12) and [k]Ctrl-I[/k] to invert the selection (Image 13).

image.caption: Image 9 - Filling in the empty space up top
Image 10 - Selecting all side edges going around the tiles
Image 11 - Beveling them with two segments
Image 12 - Selecting all faces along the beveled edges
Image 13 - Inverting the selection

content: [k]RMB,S[/k] to subdivide the selected faces with 3-4 cuts (Image 14). Delete the bottom face (Image 15). [k]O[/k] to turn on Proportional Editing, [k]Numpad0[/k] into camera view[/k] and begin randomly grabbing faces into different directions (Image 16). [k]O[/k] to turn off Proportional Editing when you're done.

image.caption: Image 14 - Subdividing the selected faces with 3-4 cuts
Image 15 - Deleting the bottom face
Image 16 - Turning on Proportional Editing, going into camera view and randomly grabbing faces in different directions

content: Add a Cube to the scene and shrink it down (Image 17). [k]/[/k] into Local View and [k]S,X[/k] to make it very thin from the side (Image 18). In Edit Mode, extrude the top face up and scale it in the y-axis (Image 19). [k]G[/k] the top face to move it, giving a bend to the geometry (Image 20).

image.caption: Image 17 - Adding a Cube to the scene and shrinking it down
Image 18 - Going into Local View and scaling it to be very thin from the side
Image 19 - Going into Edit Mode, extruding the top face up and scaling it in the y-axis
Image 20 - Moving the top face to give a bend to the geometry

content: Add a Loop Cut to the longest section and then move that Edge Loop, creating another bend (Image 21). Add a Loop Cut down the middle of the shape (Image 22). Move that Edge Loop in the z- and x-axes (Image 23). Select the vertices for the Edge Loop except the bottom and move them out to add a point to the blade (Image 24).

image.caption: Image 21 - Adding a Loop Cut to the longest section and moving that Edge Loop to create another bend
Image 22 - Adding a Loop Cut down the middle of the shape
Image 23 - Moving that Edge Loop in the z- and x-axes
Image 24 - Selecting the vertices for the Edge Loop except the bottom and moving them out to add a point to the blade

content: Select all vertices and [k]Shift-D[/k] to duplicate them (Image 25). Move the duplicates around and scale them to create a patch of grass (Image 26). Position the clump on the ground and [k]Alt-D[/k] to make several linked duplicates, covering the ground (Image 27).

image.caption: Image 25 - Selecting all vertices and duplicating them
Image 26 - Moving the duplicates around and scaling them to create a patch of grass
Image 27 - Positioning the clump on the ground and making several linked duplicates to cover the ground

compound_text: If you don't have it, install Extra Mesh Objects (

content: Enable the Add-on through [k]Edit > Preferences[/k] (Image 28). [k]Shift-A > Mesh > Extras > Rock Generator[/k] to add a rock the the scene (Image 29). [k]/[/k] to see the rock in Local View (Image 30). Apply all modifiers, then add a Decimate Modifier to bring it down to about 100 triangle (Image 31). Create several linked duplicates of the rocks and position them so they poke through the sides of the tile (Image 32).

image.caption: Image 28 - Installing Extra Mesh Objects and enabling the Add-on through Edit > Preferences
Image 29 - Adding a rock to the scene using Shift-A > Mesh > Extras > Rock Generator
Image 30 - Going into Local View to see the rock
Image 31 - Applying all modifiers and adding a Decimate Modifier to bring it down to about 100 triangles
Image 32 - Creating several linked duplicates of the rocks and positioning them so they poke through the sides of the tile

content: Select all meshes and [k]Shift-D,Y,3.5[/k] to duplicate them to the side [k]Z,1[/k] to move them up (Image 33). Select the bottom edge of the bottom and [k]E,Z,1[/k] to extrude it down (Image 34). Duplicate the rocks, rotate them and place them in the bottom of the new tile (Image 35). Duplicate a rock, scale it up and move it to the top of the surface, removing any grass that is in the way (Image 36).

image.caption: Image 33 - Selecting all meshes and duplicating them to the side and moving them up
Image 34 - Selecting the bottom edge of the bottom and extruding it down
Image 35 - Duplicating the rocks, rotating them and placing them in the bottom of the new tile
Image 36 - Duplicating a rock, scaling it up and moving it to the top of the surface, removing any grass that is in the way

content: Select the ground, isolate it in Local View and select a top face (Image 37). [k]Ctrl-Numpad+[/k] to select more until you have selected the entire top (Image 38). [k]Shift-D,RMB[/k], [k]P,S[/k] to duplicate and separate the geometry (Image 39). Move the new mesh to the World Origin, and add an Array Modifier in the x-axis and a second in the y (Image 40). Move the water tile around until there is no empty space in the camera background (Image 41).

image.caption: Image 37 - Selecting the ground, isolating it in Local View and selecting a top face
Image 38 - Expanding the selection until the entire top is selected
Image 39 - Duplicating and separating the geometry
Image 40 - Moving the new mesh to the World Origin and adding an Array Modifier in the x-axis and a second in the y-axis
Image 41 - Moving the water tile around until there is no empty space in the camera background

content: Add a cube to the scene, move it to the end of a tile and scale it until it is like a post (Image 42). [k]Alt-D,Y[/k], [k]Alt-D,X[/k] to make 2 sets of posts evenly spaced (Image 43). [k]Shift-D,RMB[/k] to duplicate a post in place, [k]R,X,90[/k] to rotate it, and the scale it to the size of a board and move it to the front of the dock (Image 44).

image.caption: Image 42 - Adding a cube to the scene, moving it to the end of a tile and scaling it until it is like a post
Image 43 - Making 2 sets of posts evenly spaced using linked duplicates in the y- and x-axes
Image 44 - Duplicating a post in place, rotating it 90 degrees in the x-axis, scaling it to the size of a board and moving it to the front of the dock

content: [k]Shift-D[/k] to add duplicates until you reach the end of the dock (Image 45). Use Loop Cuts and Bevels to add some notches and wobbles to the geometry (Image 46). Duplicate a post again, and add more structure to the dock (Image 47). Extrude the top face of one of the posts and scale it in to add a cap (if these were linked duplicates, changing affects all) (Image 48).

image.caption: Image 45 - Adding duplicates until reaching the end of the dock
Image 46 - Using Loop Cuts and Bevels to add some notches and wobbles to the geometry
Image 47 - Duplicating a post again and adding more structure to the dock
Image 48 - Extruding the top face of one of the posts and scaling it in to add a cap

content: Assign appropriate materials to all geometry (Image 49). [k]F12[/k] to render (Image 50).

image.caption: Image 49 - Assigning appropriate materials to all geometry
Image 50 - Rendering the scene

content: Add a cube to the scene, [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode, and [k]Ctrl-R[/k] to add a Loop Cut (Image 1). Select the top-left edge and [k]E[/k] to extrude it out a little bit past one square's size (Image 2). To help, you can enable [k]Snap > Snap Target > Grid[/k] to use the grid as your target (Image 3). Add a Loop Cut on the right of the new section (Image 4).

image.caption: Image 1 - Adding a cube to the scene, going into Edit Mode, and adding a Loop Cut
Image 2 - Selecting the top-left edge and extruding it out a little bit past one square's size
Image 3 - Enabling Snap > Snap Target > Grid to use the grid as a target
Image 4 - Adding a Loop Cut on the right of the new section

content: Extrude a section lower than the starting cube (Image 5). Extrude again down, then right, and then up, snaking around the starting cube (Image 6). Select all outer edges (Image 7). [k]Ctrl-B[/k] to bevel the edges with three segments (Image 8). Go to the vertices above the inner bend and [k]M,A[/k] to merge them at the center to reduce the number of triangles (Image 9).

image.caption: Image 5 - Extruding a section lower than the starting cube
Image 6 - Extruding again down, then right, and then up, snaking around the starting cube
Image 7 - Selecting all outer edges
Image 8 - Beveling the edges with three segments
Image 9 - Going to the vertices above the inner bend and merging them at the center to reduce the number of triangles

content: In Object Mode, [k]Numpad1[/k] into Front View and rotate the mesh (Image 10). [k]Numpad7[/k] into Top View, [k]Alt-D[/k] to create a linked duplicate, and move it over to the side and rotate (Image 11). Create another linked duplicate, rotating and moving to the side (Image 12). Add a Cube to the scene, select the outer edges and bevel them with three segments (Image 13). Create 10-15 linked duplicates and [k]G[/k], [k]R[/k], [k]S[/k] them around the scene (Image 14).

image.caption: Image 10 - Going to Object Mode, going to Front View and rotating the mesh
Image 11 - Going to Top View, creating a linked duplicate and moving it over to the side and rotating
Image 12 - Creating another linked duplicate, rotating and moving it to the side
Image 13 - Adding a Cube to the scene, selecting the outer edges and beveling them with three segments
Image 14 - Creating 10-15 linked duplicates and moving, rotating, and scaling them around the scene

content: Add a Circle to the scene, and [k]E,Z[/k] to extrude it up (Image 15). Add two Loop Cuts and then scale in the edges to taper the trunk (Image 16). Add a two Loop Cuts in the middle and [k]G,G[/k] to Edge Slide them closer (Image 17).

image.caption: Image 15 - Adding a Circle to the scene and extruding it up
Image 16 - Adding two Loop Cuts and scaling in the edges to taper the trunk
Image 17 - Adding two Loop Cuts in the middle and Edge Sliding them closer together

content: Select one of the faces and extrude it out several times, scaling and changing directions to make it look like a branch (Image 18). Add two more Loop Cuts to the branch and extrude one of the faces on the side, forking the branch (Image 19). Select the branch geometry, [k]Shift-D[/k] and move it around to the other side to make a second branch (Image 20). Select random edges around the bottom and [k]G,Shift-Z[/k] to add some variation to the trunk (Image 21).

image.caption: Image 18 - Selecting one of the faces and extruding it out several times, scaling and changing directions to make it look like a branch
Image 19 - Adding two more Loop Cuts to the branch and extruding one of the faces on the side to fork the branch
Image 20 - Selecting the branch geometry, duplicating and moving it around to the other side to make a second branch
Image 21 - Selecting random edges around the bottom and moving them to add some variation to the trunk

content: Add a Cube to the scene, go into Local View and scale it down in the z-axis (Image 22). [k]E,RMB[/k], [k]S[/k], [k]E[/k] the top face to extrude it, scale it, and extrude again to make a top layer (Image 23). Select all edges and bevel them (Image 24).

image.caption: Image 22 - Adding a Cube to the scene, going into Local View and scaling it down in the z-axis
Image 23 - Extruding the top face, scaling it, and extruding again to make a top layer
Image 24 - Selecting all edges and beveling them

content: Exit Local View and move the ground in place, scaling it up to cover the tree and its foliage (Image 25). Add another cube to the scene and bevel the edges (Image 26). Create several linked duplicates and embed them in the side of the ground (Image 27).

image.caption: Image 25 - Exiting Local View and moving the ground into place, scaling it up to cover the tree and its foliage
Image 26 - Adding another cube to the scene and beveling the edges
Image 27 - Creating several linked duplicates and embedding them in the side of the ground

content: Add a Cube to the scene, go into Local View and scale it down in the y-axis and scale the top in the x-axis (Image 28). Scale it down, [k]Alt-D[/k] to duplicate and create a clump of grass (Image 29). Create several clumps around the scene (Image 30).

image.caption: Image 28 - Adding a Cube to the scene, going into Local View and scaling it down in the y-axis and scaling the top in the x-axis
Image 29 - Scaling it down and creating a clump of grass using linked duplicates
Image 30 - Creating several clumps around the scene

content: Assign appropriate materials to all geometry (Image 31). [k]F12[/k] to render (Image 32).

image.caption: Image 31 - Assigning appropriate materials to all geometry
Image 32 - Rendering the scene
